questions.q: How does Python mark which lines belong inside an if, for, or while block?
options: By curly braces { }
By consistent indentation (typically 4 spaces) — indentation is the syntax, not a style choice
By a semicolon at the end of the block
Python doesn't require any marking at all
questions.explain: Python uses indentation itself to define code blocks; inconsistent indentation raises an IndentationError.

questions.q: In an if / elif / else chain, how does Python decide which branch to run?
options: It picks a branch at random
It always runs the else branch last regardless of other conditions
It runs every branch whose condition is true
It runs the first condition, top to bottom, that evaluates to true, then skips the rest
questions.explain: Python checks conditions top to bottom and stops at the first true one; else only runs if nothing else matched.

questions.q: What does `for model in models:` do?
options: Only works if models contains exactly one item
Creates a new empty list called models
Repeats the loop body once for each item in the models collection
Runs the loop body exactly once, regardless of how many items are in models
questions.explain: A for loop walks through every item in an iterable, running its body once per item.

questions.q: When is a while loop a better fit than a for loop?
options: Only when working with strings
When you don't know in advance how many times you'll need to repeat, like retrying a failed API call
While loops are never appropriate in modern Python
When you need to loop over a fixed, known list of items
questions.explain: while loops run until a condition becomes false, which fits situations where the repeat count isn't known ahead of time.

questions.q: What's the difference between break and continue inside a loop?
options: continue exits the loop entirely; break skips to the next iteration
break only works in while loops, continue only in for loops
They do exactly the same thing
break exits the loop entirely; continue skips the rest of the current iteration and moves to the next one
questions.explain: break stops the loop immediately, while continue just skips ahead to the next iteration without ending the loop.
